title: Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist (CKS) Hardening & Defense
summary: Master CKS security engineering: Pod Security Standards (Privileged, Baseline, Restricted), container securityContext hardening, AppArmor, Seccomp profiles, and Falco runtime behavioral threat detection.
learningObjectives: Enforce declarative Pod Security Admission (PSA) standards across namespaces using admission label synchronization.
Harden container workloads with least-privilege securityContext controls (allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, runAsNonRoot, dropping ALL capabilities).
Detect and mitigate container runtime threats, privilege escalation vectors, and unauthorized terminal shells using Falco behavioral rules.

curriculumModules.title: Pod Security Standards (PSA) & Admission Controllers
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Pod Security Admission replaces PodSecurityPolicies, categorizing workload isolation into Privileged, Baseline, and Restricted levels via namespace labels (pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted).
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Enforce restricted PSA on all application namespaces; reserve baseline only for system daemonsets requiring host networking, and forbid privileged entirely on worker nodes.

curriculumModules.title: Container SecurityContext & Linux Kernel Sandboxing
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: The container securityContext controls DAC permissions, privilege escalation, Linux capabilities, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and Seccomp syscall filtering (RuntimeDefault or custom profiles).
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Mandate allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, drop ALL Linux capabilities, run as an unprivileged UID (>10000), and mount /tmp and cache directories as non-executable emptyDir volumes.

curriculumModules.title: Runtime Threat Detection & Behavioral Auditing with Falco
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Falco uses eBPF kernel probes to inspect system calls at runtime, alerting on anomalous events (terminal shell spawned inside container, sensitive file access /etc/shadow, package manager execution).
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Stream Falco JSON alerts into SIEM / Loki with Falcosidekick and configure automated incident response webhooks to quarantine compromised pods via NetworkPolicy.

labs.title: Hardening Workloads with Restricted Pod Security Standards
labs.scenario: Enforce Pod Security Standards in namespace sec-restricted: label the namespace with pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted, and deploy a compliant hardened Pod secure-vault with runAsNonRoot: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities.drop: ['ALL'], and readOnlyRootFilesystem: true.
labs.productionContext: CKS hardening standards require production workloads to run with immutable root filesystems, non-root users, and zero ambient kernel capabilities to prevent container breakout.
objectives: Create namespace sec-restricted with restricted PSA enforcement label
Deploy hardened Pod secure-vault compliant with restricted PSA
Verify all capabilities are dropped and root filesystem is read-only
Validate pod compliance using pod_security_standard validation rule

steps.title: Create Security Namespace
steps.instruction: Create namespace `sec-restricted` using `kubectl create namespace sec-restricted`.

steps.title: Enforce Restricted PSA Label
steps.instruction: Apply restricted Pod Security Admission label to `sec-restricted`.

steps.title: Author Hardened Pod Manifest
steps.instruction: Create `/home/learner/secure-vault.yaml` with non-root security context and dropped capabilities.

validationRules.description: Created secure-vault Pod in sec-restricted namespace
validationRules.name: secure-vault
validationRules.remediation: Apply secure-vault Pod in namespace sec-restricted.

validationRules.description: Pod secure-vault complies with restricted Pod Security Standards
validationRules.name: secure-vault
validationRules.remediation: Set runAsNonRoot: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, and drop ALL capabilities.

validationRules.description: Verified Pod secure-vault reaches Running status
validationRules.name: secure-vault

solutionCommands:
echo -e "apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-vault
  namespace: sec-restricted
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 10001
  containers:
  - name: vault
    image: cgr.dev/chainguard/static:latest
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    securityContext:
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      capabilities:
        drop:
        - ALL" > /home/learner/secure-vault.yaml
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Verify namespace sec-restricted is labeled with pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted, and Pod secure-vault sets runAsNonRoot: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, and drop: ['ALL'].

labs.title: Falco Behavioral Threat Detection & Container Runtime Isolation
labs.scenario: Deploy an intrusion detection policy and monitor container runtime events in namespace sec-runtime. Execute a Falco simulation audit to detect unauthorized interactive shells, and apply an immutable isolation NetworkPolicy quarantine-policy restricting egress traffic from compromised pods.
labs.productionContext: Real-time threat detection allows security operations centers (SOC) to identify active attackers within seconds of container compromise before lateral movement occurs.
objectives: Create namespace sec-runtime for runtime threat monitoring
Apply isolation NetworkPolicy quarantine-policy isolating suspicious workloads

steps.title: Create Runtime Namespace
steps.instruction: Create namespace `sec-runtime` using `kubectl create namespace sec-runtime`.

steps.title: Apply Quarantine NetworkPolicy
steps.instruction: Create `/home/learner/quarantine.yaml` isolating `suspicious-workload` from network egress and apply it.

validationRules.description: Applied quarantine NetworkPolicy isolating compromised workload
validationRules.name: quarantine-policy
validationRules.remediation: Apply NetworkPolicy quarantine-policy in namespace sec-runtime.

solutionCommands:
echo -e "apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: quarantine-policy
  namespace: sec-runtime
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: suspicious-workload
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress" > /home/learner/quarantine.yaml
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure namespace sec-runtime exists, deploy suspicious-workload, run falco --version, and apply quarantine-policy NetworkPolicy.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which Linux kernel feature does Falco utilize to inspect system calls and detect anomalous runtime container behavior with minimal CPU overhead?
options: (Recommended) Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) tracepoints and kernel probes.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Falco leverages modern eBPF kernel probes to attach to system call tracepoints directly in kernel space, filtering events asynchronously with sub-millisecond latency and near-zero host CPU overhead.

assessmentQuestions.question: Under the Kubernetes Pod Security Standard (PSA) 'restricted' profile, which capability configuration is mandatory for all container securityContext definitions?
options: (Recommended) Containers must drop all capabilities by configuring capabilities.drop: ['ALL'], only optionally re-adding NET_BIND_SERVICE if needed.
Containers must add SYS_ADMIN capability to allow kernel logging.
Containers are forbidden from modifying capabilities and must leave the list empty.
Containers must drop only NET_ADMIN capability while retaining all others.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: The restricted Pod Security Standard strictly enforces least privilege by requiring all containers to drop ALL capabilities (capabilities.drop: ['ALL']). Only NET_BIND_SERVICE may optionally be re-added if binding to unprivileged ports.
